text:
Sampled HR@10 measures performance within the fixed 100-item candidate sets; it does not reliably preserve full-catalog model rankings ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). For this benchmark, retain identical users and negatives across comparisons. Recommended uncertainty analysis: compute paired per-user hit differences, bootstrap users within each category, and average the four category differences in each replicate. With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals describe uncertainty conditional on the fitted models and sampled candidates, not training-seed variability or full-catalog performance.

Repeatedly selecting the best checkpoint or configuration on the same validation users creates selection optimism; model-selection noise can rival differences between algorithms ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Predeclare the configurations, evaluation cadence, checkpoint rule and GPU-second allocation; count all attempted runs. A confidence interval computed after selecting the winner does not remove that selection bias. Keep held-out evaluation exclusively for the host’s final assessment.

Recommended controlled ablation: a 2×2 design crossing baseline versus terminal-prefix masking with baseline versus multi-negative candidate-softmax loss. Preserve the BERT4Rec backbone, optimizer, seeds, splits and inference; keep each masked target absent from the bidirectional input, consistent with [BERT4Rec’s Cloze objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690). Compare masking effects under each loss, loss effects under each masking scheme, and their interaction. Allocate equal GPU-second caps with the same epoch/batch ceilings; report actual updates and masked-target counts because compute matching can change training exposure. Each cell trains one independent model per category; never combine predictions. This design is a methodological recommendation, not evidence that either modification improves HR@10.
